name: Arnold and Libby’s radiocarbon age checks
description: Arnold and Libby compared radiocarbon age estimates with independently dated materials to assess a new archaeological dating method.

impact.note: The checks against known ages that made radiocarbon dating credible; archaeologists and earth scientists gained absolute dates and a dating field grew from it.

date.basis: Year of the dated publication, or a broad historian-estimated composition interval; no first discovery claimed.

events.statement: Arnold and Libby published checks using materials of independently known age in December 1949.

evidence.supports: The 1949 bibliographic record identifies Arnold and Libby and dates their known-age comparison paper.
The ACS history describes comparison against independently dated objects and tree growth rings.
The Texas history reports Viking Fund backing soon after a 1947 conference, distinct from the 1948 meeting.

caveats: Radiocarbon dating developed over earlier studies, and dates require calibration and attention to sample context. The full 1949 paper was not inspected; the ACS and Texas histories explain the work.
